title: Daffy Duck Is Back on the Big Screen in a Brand-New Looney Tunes Short
summary:
Daffy Duck is heading back to movie theaters. A brand-new Looney Tunes short called "Daffy Season" plays before screenings of "The Cat in the Hat," opening Friday from Warner Bros. Pictures. It is the first theatrically released Looney Tunes short since "Daffy's Rhapsody" played before "Journey 2: The Mysterious Island" in 2012.

The seven-minute short centers on Daffy Duck, voiced by Eric Bauza. He turns his beak up at his fellow Tunes as they mindlessly obsess over the game of soccer. Jeff Bergman voices Bugs Bunny, Gabriel Iglesias voices Speedy Gonzales, and Jeannie Tirado voices Lola Bunny. Todd Wilderman and Hamish Grieve are the co-directors.

A representative for the studio confirmed that the short is Bauza's final Looney Tunes movie. Bauza is also credited with additional voices for "The Cat in the Hat." Over the past 15 years, Bauza became the defining voice of modern Looney Tunes, lending his voice to Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Elmer Fudd, Foghorn Leghorn, Tweety, and Porky Pig. His other Looney Tunes credits include the series "Looney Tunes Cartoons" and the films "The Day the Earth Blew Up: A Looney Tunes Movie" and "Space Jam: A New Legacy." He also starred in "Coyote vs. Acme," a film once deemed unreleasable that later grossed $101 million worldwide.

Bauza died at his home in Los Angeles on October 25. In a tribute, Warner Bros. Pictures Animation producer Susan Rogers credited him with playing a huge role in reviving Looney Tunes. "There wasn't a single short he couldn't quote or couldn't reference," she said. "I don't think you replace Eric Bauza. The hole he leaves is huge. There are many talented people out there, and the franchise will move on. But there's only one Eric Bauza." Organizers have launched a GoFundMe campaign to support his son, Ryker Bauza, and Ryker's mother, Jessica Borutski.
why_it_matters: The short marks both a comeback for theater cartoons and a farewell to the voice behind a generation of Looney Tunes, showing how one performer can shape characters loved around the world.

background_read: Looney Tunes is a classic cartoon series from Warner Bros. with famous characters like Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, who have entertained audiences for generations.
Short cartoons used to play in theaters before the main movie, and a new short can bring old characters back to the big screen.
Voice actors give cartoon characters their sound and personality, and one actor often voices several different characters.
When a well-loved performer dies, studios and fans often pay tribute to their work and help support their family.
